info.name: llama
info.description:
llama.cpp `llama-server` endpoints — GGUF-quantized models exposed via an OpenAI-compatible HTTP surface plus llama.cpp-native extras. Every service in `ai/llama/docker-compose.llama.yml` is a standalone llama-server; the default deploy publishes the `glm5.2` container on `localhost:8010` (see `PORT_LLAMA_GLM52` in `.env`) with model alias `glm5.2`. Set the collection variable `llama` to the direct-port base URL (default http://localhost:8010) — no auth is required on the direct port per LLAMA.md.

The 'Via LiteLLM' folder routes chat through the unified LiteLLM proxy at `{{litellm}}/v1/chat/completions` using the same `glm5.2` alias (registered in `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml` → `model_list`). LiteLLM requires bearer auth via a virtual master key.

Notes:
- `/v1/embeddings` is only mounted when `llama-server` is launched with `--embedding` (or `--pooling`). The current `glm5.2` command in `docker-compose.llama.yml` does NOT enable it, so no embeddings request is included by default. Add `--embedding` to the service `command:` block and uncomment the equivalent request if you need it.
- First request after container start is slow — llama.cpp runs a warmup pass on the first inference call (see LLAMA.md § Non-obvious constraints).
- The healthcheck has a 900 s `start_period` to cover the initial GGUF download; `/health` will 503 while the model is still loading.

variable.description: Direct-port base URL for the `glm5.2` llama-server container. Published on `${PORT_LLAMA_GLM52}` (default 8010) → container port 8000. On `ai_shared` it's http://glm5.2:8000. LLAMA.md § Quick start. No auth required — the port is meant to sit behind LiteLLM.

Model alias returned by `/v1/models` and required in the `"model"` field of chat/completion requests. Set via `-a glm5.2` in the compose `command:` block. If you add more llama-server services (see LLAMA.md § Adding more models), each one carries its own alias.
LiteLLM base URL for the 'Via LiteLLM' folder. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the `glm5.2` model. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` only by requests inside the 'Via LiteLLM' folder — direct-port requests need no auth.

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns `{"status":"ok"}` once the GGUF weights have finished loading. Returns 503 while the model is still loading — expected during the ~900 s `start_period` on first launch (initial UD-IQ1_S download is ~176 GB). LLAMA.md § No tests.

OpenAI-compatible model listing. Returns `{"object":"list","data":[{"id":"glm5.2","object":"model",...}]}` where the `id` matches the alias set via `-a` in the compose command (LLAMA.md § Configuration knobs). Use this to sanity-check that the alias the client sends in `"model"` matches what llama-server actually advertises.

llama.cpp-native server introspection. Returns default sampler params, model alias, model path, embedded chat template, build info, and enabled modalities. Handy for verifying that `--jinja` picked up GLM's chat template (LLAMA.md § Common pitfalls: forgetting `--jinja` gives raw-completion behavior).

OpenAI-compatible chat completion. Response shape mirrors OpenAI: `{id, object:"chat.completion", choices:[{message:{role,content},finish_reason}], usage:{...}}`. GLM's chat template is applied server-side because the compose command sets `--jinja` — without that flag the roles are ignored and you get raw-completion behavior (LLAMA.md § Common pitfalls). Add `"stream": true` for SSE streaming.

OpenAI-compatible chat completion with Server-Sent Events. Response is a stream of `data: {...}` chunks terminated by `data: [DONE]`, each chunk containing a `choices[0].delta.content` fragment. Postman shows the raw event stream in the response body.

OpenAI-compatible text completion (legacy, no chat template). Response shape: `{id, object:"text_completion", choices:[{text, index, finish_reason}], usage:{...}}`. Prefer `/v1/chat/completions` for anything that should honor GLM's chat template — this endpoint feeds the prompt string verbatim to the model.

llama.cpp-native completion. Distinct from `/v1/completions`: exposes llama.cpp-specific sampler knobs (`n_predict`, `mirostat`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `repeat_penalty`, `grammar`, `json_schema`, `cache_prompt`, `slot_id`, ...) that the OpenAI-shaped endpoints don't. Response shape: `{content, tokens_predicted, tokens_evaluated, timings, stop, ...}`. Add `"stream": true` for NDJSON streaming (one `{content, stop}` object per line).

llama.cpp-native tokenizer. Returns `{"tokens": [int, int, ...]}` — the model's tokenization of `content`. Pass `"add_special": true` to include BOS/EOS markers, `"with_pieces": true` to also get the string piece for each token id. Useful for context-window budgeting before firing a large completion at a 65 k-context server (see `-c 65536` in the compose command).

llama.cpp-native detokenizer. Returns `{"content": "..."}` — the string reconstructed from the token id array. Inverse of `/tokenize`. Handy when consuming logprobs or streaming diagnostics that surface raw token ids.

item.name: Via LiteLLM
item.description: Chat routed through the unified LiteLLM proxy at `{{litellm}}` instead of hitting the llama-server port directly. LiteLLM's `model_list` entry for `glm5.2` (see `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml`) forwards to `http://glm5.2:8000/v1` over the `ai_shared` Docker network. Requires bearer auth via a virtual master key — set the `virtual master key` collection variable. Use this path when you want unified logging / rate-limiting / retries / spend tracking across all backends.

request.description: Same OpenAI-compatible chat surface as the direct-port `/v1/chat/completions`, but proxied through LiteLLM. The `"model"` field must be `glm5.2` — that's the `model_name` LiteLLM matches on to route to the `openai/glm5.2` provider block. LiteLLM strips its virtual key and forwards to llama-server with `api_key: none`. Response shape is identical to the direct call. LLAMA.md § LiteLLM integration.

Streaming chat via LiteLLM. Same SSE `data: {...}` / `data: [DONE]` shape as the direct-port streaming request; LiteLLM passes chunks through as they arrive from llama-server. Look at LiteLLM logs (`docker logs litellm`) if the stream stalls — the `stream_timeout` in `litellm_config.yaml` caps how long the proxy waits between chunks.
